name: MultiTP
description: A cross-lingual corpus of moral dilemma vignettes in over 100 languages, building on the Moral Machine experiment (40 million human judgments). Tests how LLMs make moral decisions across dimensions including gender, age, fitness, social status, and species across diverse linguistic and cultural contexts. Analysis of 19 LLMs reveals inconsistent moral preferences depending on the language of the prompt.
evaluation_method: moral preference alignment (agreement with human population judgments per language/culture)
typical_sota_score: Models show significant inconsistency — moral preference scores can vary by 20–40% across languages for the same underlying dilemma
reputation: Published at ICLR 2025; builds on landmark Moral Machine experiment; 100+ language coverage; critical for understanding cross-lingual moral alignment inconsistency in LLMs
notes: ICLR 2025. Extends the Moral Machine experiment (40M human judgments from 233 countries by Awad et al.) to LLM evaluation. Core finding: LLMs display inconsistent moral preferences across languages — the same moral dilemma receives different judgments depending on the prompt language, indicating culturally inconsistent value alignment. 19 LLMs evaluated across 100+ language variants. Implies that 'alignment' achieved in English training may not transfer cross-lingually.
